title: A reliable quantum-job service on unreliable backends
description: A job service that canonicalises OpenQASM circuits, caches results by canonical hash + backend + calibration version, schedules across three simulated noisy backends, survives retries, lease expiries, an outage and recalibrations, and returns exact shot totals with error bars.
outcome: You can find and guard the seams where quantum results, at-least-once execution and service architecture meet: exact shot accounting under duplicate execution, a cache key that respects circuit equivalence and calibration versions, and a result contract that always carries uncertainty.
environment: Mac mini or Windows 11; Python 3.12 venv; numpy 2.5.3; stdlib otherwise. Reuses labs from quantum-computing (L100 #5, L300 #12-13, L400 #17, _shared/qsim), distributed-systems (L200 #7) and application-architecture (L300 #13, #15, L400 #21) through _kb.py. Discrete-event simulation on a fake clock. SDK path (pending CI): a Qiskit Aer backend behind the same Backend interface - not built.
overview: Submit -> canonicalise -> versioned cache -> scheduler -> per-backend queues behind bulkheads and breakers -> leased, fenced chunk attempts -> result with error bars.
The interesting bugs are at the seams: a redelivered chunk inflates N, two texts of one circuit miss the cache, a recalibration stales cached results, a result without uncertainty misleads.
prerequisites: quantum-computing L400 #17 (orchestrator, backend adapter) and L300 #12-13 (noise, readout mitigation)
distributed-systems L200 #7 (leases, fencing tokens), L200 #8 (at-least-once), L100 #5 (idempotency keys), L200 #10 (cache invalidation)
application-architecture L300 #13 (circuit breaker, bulkhead), L300 #15 (percentiles), L400 #21 (Little's law, headroom)

designBrief.context: Clients submit small OpenQASM circuits (2-4 qubits) with shots, a seed and a minimum estimated fidelity. Three backends differ: fast-noisy (4 slots, 1 s/chunk), slow-clean (2 slots, 3 s/chunk, 15% of chunks 5x slower) and flaky-mid (3 slots, 25% start rejections, a 40 s outage). Two backends recalibrate during the run. Clients retry submissions.
constraints: shots returned == shots requested for 100% of jobs under injected failures
a cache hit never crosses a calibration version (0 crossings)
p95 queue time <= 30 s in the seeded 240-job load test (0.8 jobs/s)
every result carries per-outcome standard errors and its backend + calibration version
no job lands below its fidelity floor when a backend meets it
designBrief.question: How must chunk attempts, the cache key and the scheduler be designed so that duplicates, drift and outages never change what a client receives?

architecture.summary: jobservice.JobService is a discrete-event simulation on the quantum topic's FakeClock. submit() fingerprints the request (idempotency key), canonicalises the QASM (canon.py: L100 #5 reader, cancel adjacent self-inverse pairs, sorted ASAP moments) and looks up the result cache keyed on canonical hash + backend + calibration version + shots + seed. On a miss, pick() applies the fidelity floor, then a 15 s wait target, then the best estimated fidelity, and the job's 1000-shot chunks join that backend's queue. dispatch() honours the bulkhead (slots) and the backend's CircuitBreaker; each attempt gets a lease (10 s) and a fencing token. finish() executes the chunk on the L300 #12 noise model and commits it to the ledger: a FencedStorage slot per chunk, one calibration version per job (a newer version restarts the job). result() builds counts, probabilities with standard errors, and readout-mitigated values with propagated errors.

seams.contract: a chunk contributes exactly its shots once, however many attempts ran; attempts of one chunk are seeded identically
seams.risk: a lease expires on a slow backend, the chunk is redelivered, both attempts report and merged counts exceed the requested shots (4000 of 2000) with error bars that are too narrow

seams.contract: equivalent circuit texts map to one canonical hash; every rewrite keeps the unitary; inequivalent circuits never share a key
seams.risk: a raw-text key loses 38 of 108 hits; an over-eager canonicaliser would serve another circuit's result

seams.contract: every result has shots == requested, per-outcome stderr, mitigated values with propagated stderr, backend and calibration version
seams.risk: a bare count is over-read; mitigated values look exact but have larger variance (0.008486 vs 0.007898 for P(00))

seams.contract: the calibration version is part of the cache key and of each chunk commit; one result = one calibration
seams.risk: a versionless key serves 28 hits measured and mitigated under a superseded calibration; a job straddling a recalibration mixes two devices

glossary.meaning: One execution of a 1000-shot slice of a job on one backend; a chunk may have several attempts.
Time-limited right to run an attempt (10 s); when it expires the chunk is redelivered (at-least-once).
Number from one counter that only grows, attached to each attempt; the result slot rejects a write with a lower token than it has seen.
One text for all equivalent spellings of a circuit: indices instead of register names, cancelled self-inverse pairs, gates sorted inside ASAP moments.
Counter that increases each time a backend publishes new noise parameters; part of the cache key and of every chunk commit.
Client's minimum estimated fidelity; the scheduler never picks a backend below it when one meets it.
Per-backend limit on chunks in flight (slots), so one slow backend cannot hold every worker.
sqrt(p(1-p)/N) for a shot-based probability; mitigated values use the propagated covariance A^-1 Cov A^-T.

code:
"""L600 #07 - a reliable quantum-job service on unreliable backends (discrete-event simulation on a fake clock).

submit -> idempotency check -> canonicalise -> cache -> scheduler picks a backend -> chunks queue per backend
dispatch: bulkhead (slots) + circuit breaker; each chunk attempt gets a lease and a fencing token
finish:  ledger.commit (fenced, versioned) -> job complete -> result with error bars, cached by version
Faults: ledger 'lease-expiry' (shipped unfixed ledger), cache key 'stale-cache' / 'text-key' (see cachekeys.py).
"""
import hashlib
import heapq
from collections import deque

import results
from _kb import q17, resilience
from backends import TransientBackendError
from cachekeys import cache_key
from canon import canonicalise, circuit_hash

LEASE_S, CHUNK, BACKOFF_S, MAX_ATTEMPTS = 10.0, 1000, 0.5, 12
SCHED_WAIT_S = 15.0                    # scheduler's wait target: half the 30 s p95 budget (headroom)


class Conflict(ValueError):
    """Same job id, different request body (HTTP 422 in an API)."""


class JobService:
    def __init__(self, backends, ledger, key=cache_key, policy="floor+budget"):
        self.clock, self.ledger, self.key, self.policy = q17.FakeClock(), ledger, key, policy
        self.backends = {b.name: b for b in backends}
        self.queues, self.busy = {n: deque() for n in self.backends}, dict.fromkeys(self.backends, 0)
        self.retrying, self.max_busy = dict.fromkeys(self.backends, 0), dict.fromkeys(self.backends, 0)
        self.breakers = {n: resilience.CircuitBreaker(n, window=10, min_calls=5, failure_rate=0.5, open_s=20.0,
                                                      clock=lambda: self.clock.now, log=lambda r: self.log.append({"t": self.clock.now, **r}))
                         for n in self.backends}
        self.jobs, self.cache, self.events, self.seq, self.log = {}, {}, [], 0, []

    def at(self, t, fn, *args):
        self.seq += 1
        heapq.heappush(self.events, (t, self.seq, fn, args))

    def run(self):
        while self.events:
            t, _, fn, args = heapq.heappop(self.events)
            self.clock.now = max(self.clock.now, t)
            fn(*args)

    def healthy(self, name):
        br = self.breakers[name]                              # open breakers leave the pool until open_s has passed
        return br.state != "open" or self.clock.now - br.opened_at >= br.open_s

    def wait_estimate(self, name):
        b = self.backends[name]
        return (len(self.queues[name]) + self.busy[name] + self.retrying[name]) / b.slots * b.expected_latency()

    def pick(self, n, ops, floor):
        """Fidelity floor first, then the queue-time target; best estimated fidelity among what is left."""
        names = [m for m in self.backends if self.healthy(m)] or list(self.backends)
        fid = {m: self.backends[m].estimated_fidelity(n, ops) for m in names}
        if self.policy in ("best-fidelity", "fastest"):        # the two rejected options (ADR 0002)
            return max(names, key=fid.get) if self.policy == "best-fidelity" else min(names, key=self.wait_estimate)
        ok = [m for m in names if fid[m] >= floor]
        fast = [m for m in ok if self.wait_estimate(m) <= SCHED_WAIT_S]
        if fast:
            return max(fast, key=fid.get)
        return min(ok, key=self.wait_estimate) if ok else max(names, key=fid.get)

    def submit(self, req):
        body = repr(sorted(req.items())).encode("utf-8")
        fp, jid = hashlib.sha256(body).hexdigest(), req["job_id"]
        if jid in self.jobs:                                   # client retry: replay, never a second job
            if self.jobs[jid]["fp"] != fp:
                raise Conflict(f"job id {jid} already used with a different request")
            return self.jobs[jid]
        n, ops, _ = canonicalise(req["qasm"])
        chash, shots, seed = circuit_hash(req["qasm"]), req["shots"], req["seed"]
        job = {"fp": fp, "req": req, "n": n, "ops": ops, "submitted": self.clock.now, "started": None, "done": None,
               "attempts": 0, "cache_hit": None}
        self.jobs[jid] = job
        for name in sorted(self.backends, key=lambda m: -self.backends[m].estimated_fidelity(n, ops)):
            b = self.backends[name]
            hit = self.cache.get(self.key(req["qasm"], chash, b, shots, seed))
            if hit and b.estimated_fidelity(n, ops) >= req["min_fidelity"]:
                job.update(backend=name, started=self.clock.now, done=self.clock.now, source=hit["job_id"],
                           cache_hit={"cached_version": hit["version"], "current_version": b.version})
                return job
        job["backend"] = name = self.pick(n, ops, req["min_fidelity"])
        job["cache_key"] = self.key(req["qasm"], chash, self.backends[name], shots, seed)
        chunks = -(-shots // CHUNK)
        self.ledger.open(jid, chunks)
        self.queues[name].extend((jid, c, 0) for c in range(chunks))
        self.dispatch(name)
        return job

    def dispatch(self, name):
        b, q = self.backends[name], self.queues[name]
        while q and self.busy[name] < b.slots:                 # bulkhead: never more than `slots` in flight
            jid, c, tries = q.popleft()
            if self.ledger.chunk_done(jid, c) or (jid, c) in self.ledger.leases:
                continue
            try:
                run_s = self.breakers[name].call(b.start, self.clock.now)
            except (TransientBackendError, resilience.CircuitOpen) as e:
                self.jobs[jid]["attempts"] += 1
                delay = self.breakers[name].open_s if isinstance(e, resilience.CircuitOpen) else BACKOFF_S * 2 ** min(tries, 5)
                if tries + 1 >= MAX_ATTEMPTS:
                    raise RuntimeError(f"{jid} chunk {c}: {MAX_ATTEMPTS} attempts failed") from e
                self.retrying[name] += 1
                self.at(self.clock.now + delay, self.requeue, name, (jid, c, tries + 1), False, True)
                continue
            token, job = self.ledger.grant(jid, c), self.jobs[jid]
            job["attempts"] += 1
            job["started"] = job["started"] if job["started"] is not None else self.clock.now
            self.busy[name] += 1
            self.max_busy[name] = max(self.max_busy[name], self.busy[name])
            self.at(self.clock.now + run_s, self.finish, name, jid, c, token, b.version)
            self.at(self.clock.now + LEASE_S, self.expire, name, jid, c, token)

    def requeue(self, name, item, front=False, backoff=False):
        self.retrying[name] -= backoff                         # a chunk waiting out a backoff counted as load
        self.queues[name].appendleft(item) if front else self.queues[name].append(item)
        self.dispatch(name)

    def expire(self, name, jid, c, token):
        """Lease ran out before the attempt reported: assume it is lost and redeliver (at-least-once)."""
        if self.ledger.holds(jid, c, token) and not self.ledger.chunk_done(jid, c):
            self.ledger.release(jid, c)
            self.log.append({"t": self.clock.now, "evt": "lease-expired", "job": jid, "chunk": c, "token": token})
            self.requeue(name, (jid, c, 0), front=True)

    def finish(self, name, jid, c, token, version):
        self.busy[name] -= 1
        job, b = self.jobs[jid], self.backends[name]
        counts = b.execute(job["n"], job["ops"], version, min(CHUNK, job["req"]["shots"] - c * CHUNK),
                           job["req"]["seed"], c)
        status, restarted = self.ledger.commit(jid, c, token, version, counts)
        self.log.append({"t": self.clock.now, "evt": "commit", "job": jid, "chunk": c, "token": token, "status": status,
                         "restarted": restarted})
        if self.ledger.holds(jid, c, token):
            self.ledger.release(jid, c)
        for k in range(self.ledger.jobs[jid]["chunks"]):        # rejected or restarted chunks go back to the queue
            if not self.ledger.chunk_done(jid, k) and (jid, k) not in self.ledger.leases and (restarted or k == c):
                self.queues[name].append((jid, k, 0))
        if job["done"] is None and self.ledger.complete(jid):
            job["done"] = self.clock.now
            self.cache[job["cache_key"]] = {"job_id": jid, "version": self.ledger.jobs[jid]["version"]}
        self.dispatch(name)

    def result(self, jid):
        job = self.jobs[jid]
        src = job.get("source", jid)                            # a cache hit reads the job that produced the result
        v = self.ledger.jobs[src]["version"]
        return results.build(jid, self.ledger.counts(src), job["n"], self.backends[job["backend"]].readout(job["n"], v),
                             job["backend"], v, cache_hit=job["cache_hit"] is not None)

codeWalkthrough.title: Events on a fake clock
codeWalkthrough.detail: at() pushes (time, seq, fn, args) on a heap and run() pops them in order; the clock is the quantum L400 #17 FakeClock, so a 15 s slow chunk costs no real time and every run is identical.

codeWalkthrough.title: submit(): idempotency, canonical hash, cache
codeWalkthrough.detail: The request fingerprint decides replay vs Conflict for a known job_id. canonicalise() feeds circuit_hash(); the cache is checked on every backend that meets the floor, best fidelity first, with the key from cachekeys (hash, backend, calibration version, shots, seed).

codeWalkthrough.title: pick(): floor, wait target, fidelity
codeWalkthrough.detail: Healthy backends (breaker not open, or open longer than open_s) that meet the floor and whose wait estimate ((queued + running + backing-off chunks) / slots x expected latency) is under 15 s; the best estimated fidelity among them. The two rejected policies stay for try_it.

codeWalkthrough.title: dispatch(): bulkhead, breaker, lease
codeWalkthrough.detail: At most `slots` chunks in flight. The start goes through CircuitBreaker.call; a TransientBackendError backs off exponentially, CircuitOpen waits open_s. A started attempt gets a fencing token and two events: finish at its run time, expire at LEASE_S.

codeWalkthrough.title: expire(): at-least-once redelivery
codeWalkthrough.detail: If the attempt still holds the lease and the chunk has no result, the lease is released and the chunk goes to the front of the queue. The slow attempt keeps running - this is where duplicates come from.

codeWalkthrough.title: finish(): fenced, versioned commit
codeWalkthrough.detail: The chunk runs on the backend's noise model with a seed from (seed, chunk, version, circuit, backend). ledger.commit() rejects a stale token or an older calibration, restarts the job on a newer one, and requeues anything not done; the first complete job fills the cache.

codeWalkthrough.title: result(): uncertainty travels with the counts
codeWalkthrough.detail: results.build() returns counts, probabilities with standard errors, readout-mitigated values (L300 #13) with propagated errors, the backend and the calibration version; a cache hit reads the producing job's ledger.

inRealSystems: Cloud quantum services queue jobs per device, publish calibration data with timestamps (e.g. BackendProperties.last_update_date) and retry transient failures; the shot-accounting and calibration-version seams apply to any client or broker built on them.
Message brokers deliver at least once (visibility or consumer timeouts); fencing at the result store is how duplicate work becomes harmless.
Result caches for expensive computations key on a canonical form of the input plus the version of everything the result depends on.
useWhen: Use this shape - idempotent intake, canonical + versioned cache key, chunked attempts with leases and fencing, a result contract with uncertainty - whenever expensive, statistical jobs run on shared, drifting, failing backends. Avoid it for one-off interactive runs where a single synchronous call and no cache is simpler.
simulatorVsReal: Backends are the numpy density-matrix simulator with illustrative noise, latency and failure values on a fake clock; recalibration is a scripted event. Real devices publish per-qubit calibration on their own schedule, have much longer queues, and need transpilation; the seams and tests stay the same. Pending CI: a Qiskit Aer backend behind the Backend interface (not built).
caution: Fencing makes duplicates harmless only if every write path checks the token; one unchecked path reintroduces the bug. Never expose a job service or its result store beyond 127.0.0.1 without authentication, and never put credentials into circuit text or job ids (they become cache keys and logs).
checkpoint: PASS if run_project.py prints 5/5, 4/4, 3/3 and exits 0, each --inject fault exits 1 on the lines that guard its seam, and you can explain why a lease alone does not prevent duplicate shots.

checkYourself.q: The lease-expired attempt and its redelivery both finish. Why do the fixed totals stay exact whichever arrives first?
checkYourself.a: Both attempts of a chunk use the same seed, so their counts are identical, and the slot replaces rather than adds; a lower token arriving later is rejected.

checkYourself.q: Why is the calibration version in the cache key and not just a TTL?
checkYourself.a: A TTL guesses when a result goes stale; the version says exactly when the device changed. Without it, 28 hits crossed a recalibration.

checkYourself.q: Why did best-fidelity fail the latency budget?
checkYourself.a: It sent all 240 jobs to slow-clean (2 slots, about 4.9 s expected per chunk), so the queue kept growing: p95 1163.38 s.

checkYourself.q: Mitigation lowered the TVD from 0.0653 to 0.0098. Why must the result still report a larger standard error?
checkYourself.a: The inverse assignment matrix amplifies shot noise: the stderr of P(00) grows from 0.007898 to 0.008486.

scalingLimits: One token counter per service: several coordinators with private counters can issue equal or lower tokens for the same chunk (signal: two accepted commits for one chunk, shots_returned > shots_requested).

Dense readout mitigation is 2^n x 2^n: the matrix and its inverse grow exponentially and mitigated variance with them (signal: mitigated stderr far above raw, negative quasi-probabilities); move to tensored or subspace mitigation.
The wait estimate is a model; slow tails and outages make it optimistic (signal: max queue time 38.5 s against the 15 s target; p95 creeping toward the 30 s budget as load rises).

conceptSummary: A quantum result is a statistic tied to one calibration; a job service delivers work at least once. Where they meet, a redelivered chunk inflates N, two texts of one circuit miss the cache, a recalibration stales cached results and a bare count hides its uncertainty. Fenced, idempotent chunk attempts, a canonical + versioned cache key, a floor-then-wait scheduler and a result contract with error bars keep 240/240 jobs exact, 0 cache hits across versions and p95 at 18.38 s.

experiments.title: Qiskit Aer behind the existing Backend interface
experiments.why: KNOWN-GAPS lists the Qiskit cross-check for 07 as not run. If a real simulator SDK fits the interface, the service's reliability machinery (leases, fencing, cache keys by calibration version) is shown to be independent of the backend implementation.

steps.title: Conformance and agreement
steps.detail: AerBackend overrides only exact_probs (Aer density matrix + readout matrix) and execute (Aer sampling with ReadoutError, seed_simulator from the same (seed, chunk, version, circuit, backend) tuple). conformance() checks counts, determinism per attempt, normalisation, versions, and exact TVD to the numpy backend.
steps.mac:
cd integrated/labs/L600/07-quantum-job-service
python -m pip install qiskit==2.6.1 qiskit-aer==0.18.2
python mac_mini/aer_backend.py --out ~/kb-runs/07-aer.jsonl; echo $?
steps.expected: Three conformance lines (fast-noisy, slow-clean, flaky-mid) with every check true and exact_tvd_vs_numpy <= 1e-6; the load-test line passes with slow-clean on Aer (shots exact, 0 contract violations, p95 <= 30 s); exit 0.

experiments.measure: exact_tvd_vs_numpy per backend; load-test shots_exact, contract_violations, p95_queue_s, ci95_coverage
experiments.decides: Agreement closes the 'SDK cross-checks not run: Qiskit (07)' gap for macOS and lets the quantum topic's 'Capstone SDK swap not built' note point here; a TVD above 1e-6 means the noise model mapping (channel order, readout orientation, qubit order) is wrong, not the service.

experiments.title: Qubit walls per backend kind -> admission rule
experiments.why: The service accepts any circuit its reader parses. Memory decides the widest job each backend kind can run: 2^n x 16 B for a statevector, 4^n x 16 B for a density matrix; the numpy density-matrix path also grows ~8^n in time.

steps.title: Sweep numpy and Aer up to the computed walls
steps.detail: GHZ-n; Aer gets max_memory_mb = the mac_profile.py budget so it refuses instead of swapping.
steps.expected: Walls from mac_profile budgets: statevector 29 (16 GB), 30 (24/32 GB), 31 (64 GB); density matrix 14 (16 GB), 15 (24-64 GB). Aer runs up to the wall and errors at wall + 1; numpy density matrix stops on the time cap first.

experiments.measure: largest n per backend kind; seconds per n; the error at wall + 1
experiments.decides: Admission: the job service refuses at submit (422-style) any job wider than the wall of the backend kind it would run on, instead of queueing work that can only fail or swap; today's circuits (<= 4 qubits) are far inside it.

experiments.title: The load test over many seeds and larger fleets
experiments.why: The scorecard's p95 fitness function is checked on one seeded run. The sandbox shows seed 7 passing (p95 18.4 s) and seed 8 failing (p95 170.5 s) with the same fleet: one seed is a sample, not a capacity guarantee.

steps.title: 40 seeds x fleets of 3, 6 and 12 backends
steps.detail: loadtest.run() unchanged; fleets = backends.fleet() plus renamed copies; arrival rate 0.8 x copies keeps the load per backend constant; one spawn worker per performance core.
steps.expected: contract_violations 0 in every run (exit 0); fitness_pass_rate per fleet size in the summary lines, worst and median p95.

experiments.measure: fitness_pass_rate, worst_p95_queue_s and median_p95_queue_s per fleet size; lease_expiries and rejected_commits per run
experiments.decides: The p95 fitness function is judged over seeds (e.g. >= 95 % of 40 seeds) and ADR 0002 records the capacity (backends per offered load) that meets it; contract invariants stay 100 %.

macMini.overnight: caffeinate -i python mac_mini/overnight_load.py --seeds 40 --jobs 5000 --copies 1 2 4: 120 runs of 5,000 jobs in parallel processes. It reveals the tail a single seeded run hides: how often breakers open, how many lease expiries end in a fenced (rejected) commit, and the spread of p95 from seed to seed.
